correctness.rationale: For all \(n\ge3\) and \(h>0\), the centered Green function is constructed by solving the Kirchhoff point Poisson equation. Fourier diagonalization yields the exact vertex Green diagonal and both edge-endpoint resistances. Both continuum quadratic coefficients are proved strictly positive; a two-high-mode derivative bound establishes the unique positive crossover, all edge-midpoint extremizers and strict rank monotonicity. A uniform Fourier series establishes the golden-ratio limit and first \(n^{-1}\) term. Separately formulated refined-graph exact-rational Poisson solves reproduced 60 predicted point evaluations \(n\in\{3,4,5,6\}\), \(h\in\{1/3,1,5/2\}\). No finite check is used as an infinite proof.

originality.rationale: The mathematical claim is the exact one-parameter sharp continuous embedding and its unique, \(n\)-monotone rim-to-rung localization threshold, not the classical Green resistance formula or any equilateral resistance table. The strongest relevant full primary text, Cinkir 2017, explicitly restricts to \(h=1\) and vertex resistance/Kirchhoff index. Baker–Faber is general calculus; Cinkir 2015 an open unit ladder; Usman 2018 general nonsharp Sobolev estimates. The indexed mathematical-record searches identified nearby weighted ladder and prism research but not a stronger covering statement. Unindexed implicit results remain a priority risk.
residual_risks: A generalized but unindexed weighted-quantum-graph formula could imply the threshold through an elementary specialization; no claim of exhaustive novelty is made.
The literature comparison, even with accessible primary full texts, is not independent bibliographic review.
The equilateral \(h=1\) spectral/resistance identities are known antecedents and are excluded from any priority assertion.

value.rationale: Sharp uniform first-order Sobolev stability on a natural weighted cyclic graph family is an independently motivated variational quantity, with applications to optimal observation locations. The result solves this family in all dimensions and all positive rung lengths, establishes a strict single transition and complete equality cases, and discovers the quantitative golden-ratio threshold law with a first-order finite-size correction. The exact two-term edge-displacement deficit and rational rung-dominant branch make the result structurally informative rather than a single tabulated constant.
